summary: nlargest returns up to n largest items as a list in descending order.
documentation: nlargest returns up to n largest items as a list in descending order. For a small requested count relative to a large iterable, heap selection avoids sorting the entire collection. An optional key selects the comparison value.
inputs: An object with scores (list of integers) and n (integer 0..100).
returns: Up to n scores in descending order, retaining duplicates.
caution: This does not deduplicate equal values. Sorting may be simpler or faster when n is large relative to the data.
scenarios: Show a short leaderboard from a larger local score list.
Choose the largest outstanding job sizes for review.
Extract the most expensive quote amounts from an import.
title: Select the top scores
problem: Input is {scores, n}, with integer scores and n 0..100. Return up to n largest scores in descending order, preserving duplicate values.
goal: Use heapq.nlargest() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Import nlargest from heapq and pass n before scores.
